title: ADP Payroll Pricing for Small Businesses in 2026
summary: ADP payroll pricing includes plan fees, per-employee charges, and add-ons that make up your total bill. See the breakdown to estimate what you'll pay.
body_markdown:
## Automating the data that feeds ADP payroll with Activepieces


Don't expect Activepieces, an MIT-licensed automation platform with 746+ integrations, to run payroll or lower ADP's price. It moves the approved inputs into ADP so fewer errors and off-cycle runs land on your invoice.


Those line items, in turn, are the ones the quote above made visible.


### Which ADP payroll data handoffs to automate


Price a payroll run backward from what it costs when it goes wrong.


A missed timesheet, a new hire keyed in late, or an expense approval that never reached payroll each tends to become a correction or an off-cycle run, and whoever absorbs that extra work quietly subsidizes a client on a shared account.


Automate three handoffs: approved timesheets passing into payroll input, new-hire records created once and carried into ADP, and expense approvals reaching the run before it closes.


A fourth item's an alert rather than a handoff. A late-run warning goes to Slack, the team chat tool, so someone sees a stalled run while it can still be fixed.


### A timesheet-to-payroll workflow


In the flow below, approvals, new-hire records and expense approvals pass through an Activepieces flow into ADP payroll input, with a late-run alert going to Slack. Take from it the label that matters: it doesn't run payroll.


Flows are unlimited on every Activepieces plan, including the free one, so a flow like this doesn't depend on which tier you pick.


ADP still calculates, files and pays; Activepieces only delivers what ADP needs, once someone has approved it, and at 1 credit a run the Free plan's 1,000 monthly credits cover 1,000 such runs.


In practice, the trigger is the approval itself. The flow checks that required fields are present, writes the record to the payroll input, and posts to Slack if the run hasn't been confirmed by your internal cutoff.


Which ADP connection you can use depends on your plan and what ADP enables for your account, so confirm that before you design around it.


That check belongs in your quote conversation, not after signing.


Skip it when headcount's small and changes are rare, because a few manual entries a cycle cost less than building and maintaining a flow.


Skip it too when approvals happen by email or in conversation with no consistent record; automation will only move the mess faster. Fix the approval habit first, then automate the handoff.
